content.text:
I restored the three items, and `openspec validate --strict` still passes.

## Restored
- **Response envelope.** Decision 8 says every response carries a request ID, plus either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message. The API spec has a new "Response envelope" requirement, and task 4.3 tests it on every route.
- **HTTP codes.** These are back to the original set of 401, 404, 409, 422 and 503. The original listed five statuses without saying which error got which, so the mapping is my reading:
  - 401: `unauthenticated`
  - 404: `not_found`
  - 409: `content_unavailable`
  - 422: `invalid_request` and `result_too_large`, told apart by the code in the envelope
  - 503: `dependency_error`

  The 403 `forbidden` I'd added is gone, so a plugin-session token now gets 401 `unauthenticated`.
- **Zod schemas.** They live in `packages/database` and serve three purposes: the API validates requests with them, the MCP generates its tool input definitions from them, and the API docs are checked against them. Tasks 4.1, 5.4 and 6.3 cover this.

## Explained (not restored)

**API log redaction**
- **Original:** keep the `Authorization` header out of the application, hosting and proxy logs, and confirm it by checking one real request in the hosting logs.
- **Now:** only the route's own logs are tested.
- **Why I cut it:** the token is read-only now and expires within an hour, so a leak matters less.
- **What it guards:** the bearer token travels in that header. Whether the hosting layer (Vercel) records request headers isn't something the route controls or a unit test can see; I haven't checked it. Checking one request costs minutes, so I'd restore it.

**Excerpt fallback**
- **Original:** when a node has no full body, the excerpt falls back to the stored embedding input. For a Roam node with a description, that's the title plus the description.
- **Now:** it falls back to `content.direct`, which is the title only.
- **The cost:** the excerpt then repeats the title the result already shows. It also drops the description, which is the text that produced the match.
- **Why I changed it:** `content.direct` is already in the node payload, while the embedding input needs another join. That's a small saving, so I'd restore the original.

**Rollback**
- **Original:** rollback must not delete synced nodes, content, vectors or existing group access.
- **Why I cut it:** this change creates none of those, so a rollback has nothing to remove.
- **What it guards:** someone rolling back might "clean up" the vectors or access rows the feature read. It costs one line, so I'd restore it.

**Search warning**
- **Original:** don't copy the threshold check or the Roam experiment's filtering after the limit, and don't swap the threshold for zero.
- **Now:** Decision 6 still says to filter before the limit, use no threshold, and keep negative similarities. It no longer names the existing code that does it wrong.
- **What it guards:** `runSupabaseSemanticSearch` in `apps/roam/src/utils/discourseNodeSearchProviders.ts` limits first and then filters in the client. It's the obvious code to copy, and copying it brings back both bugs. Naming it costs one line, so I'd restore it.
Leave them out

Okay, those four stay out. The spec keeps the restored envelope, HTTP codes and Zod schemas, and still passes `openspec validate --strict`.

The only loose end is deleting `openspec/changes/headless-mcp-retrieval/README.md`, since its line is already in the proposal.

content.text:
The four areas you asked about (verbosity, correctness, simplicity, gaps) are covered. Four things are still open, roughly in order of importance.

**1. The Roam handoff spec contradicts this change.**
`Spec: MCP token handoff` (`mcp-session-access`) still says:
- the MCP gets the space account's full permissions in v0;
- restricting the MCP is a non-goal;
- the custom access token hook is deferred;
- the password settings come after v0.

This change assumes the opposite on all four, because A2 is the decision. One of the two needs updating before tickets get cut. I'd update the Roam spec, because it predates the 11-10 decision. I haven't edited the Roam page, since it's shared content.

**2. Claims I haven't checked against the code yet:**
- **Hook support.** That Supabase's access token hook gets `session_id` and can set `role` to a custom role, and that PostgREST then switches to it. Supabase documents this, but I didn't check its docs or source.
- **`refs` in the view.** That `my_concepts` exposes `refs`, so context can filter relations with an array-contains query.
- **Own-space nodes.** That `getSharedNodeByRid` returns the caller's own nodes, not only nodes from other spaces. The code suggests it does, but I haven't tested it.
- **Revoke blast radius.** How many functions rely only on `PUBLIC` for `EXECUTE`. Any of those would break when task 1.2 revokes it.

**3. Michael's call on `CrossAppNode` and `rid`.**
This is still open in the proposal, and the API contract, type filters and payloads all depend on it.

**4. No independent read.**
I wrote most of the current version, so my own review is anchored. A fresh reviewer given only the spec files and the repo would catch things I'd miss, such as gaps between the specs, the tasks and the design.

Smaller item: `README.md` still needs deleting.

why do we need to update Spec: MCP token handoff?? this is more the referential, not the spec exactly for this project. if we chose A2 then as long as the specs generated for this project chose A2 that's good no?

You're right. The handoff spec is a reference, and A2 is owned by this change. Anything A2 needs beyond the handoff should be specced here, not pushed back into the reference.

The spec mostly does that already: the hook, `mcp_reader` and the function allowlist are all owned here, in task group 1. There's one leftover, though. The password settings are worded as a dependency rather than as work this change owns:
- **Proposal Impact:** "This change needs that change's password settings in v0, not after it."
- **Design Decision 4:** "`mcp-session-access`'s password settings must ship in v0."
- **Tasks header and task 1.5:** they list the password settings as needed from `mcp-session-access`, and 1.5 only *confirms* they're on.

The handoff spec plans those settings for after v0, so as written, nothing in either spec turns them on for v0. That's a gap A2 can't have, because a read-only database role doesn't stop the session from changing the space password.

The fix is to make this change own them:
- task 1.5 becomes "Turn on `secure_password_change` in `config.toml`, and 'require current password' on the hosted project";
- the three dependency sentences drop the password settings;
- the remaining dependencies on the handoff spec are the handoff, the `mcp_session` registry and sign-out, which it does provide.

That's four small edits to `proposal.md`, `design.md` and `tasks.md`. Want me to make them?
password settings? that's not password right? just session token. if so be consistent here

Right, the MCP only holds a session token, never the password. These settings exist because of that token. Here's the threat they block:

```
MCP's session token --PUT /auth/v1/user {password: new}--> Supabase Auth
                                                              |
                     (no current password needed today)       v
                                       space password changed
                                       --> every plugin locked out
                                       --> token holder signs in with the new
                                           password and gets unregistered,
                                           writable sessions (escapes A2)
```

Supabase Auth lets any session of an account set a new password. The database role doesn't apply, because this goes through Auth, not PostgREST. The two Supabase settings close that path:
- `secure_password_change` requires reauthentication for sessions older than 24h;
- "require current password" refuses any change that doesn't include the old password, which the MCP never has.

So they aren't about the MCP using a password. They stop a token holder from replacing the password. You're right that "password settings" reads as if the MCP had one.

**Proposed consistent term:** "**password-change lock**". Decision 4 would define it once: "Supabase Auth settings that stop a session token from changing the space password: `secure_password_change` and 'require current password'." Every other mention would use that term. I'd also rename the requirement "Handed-over sessions cannot change the space password" to keep its wording but add "using only its session token".

**Edits I'd make**, combining this with the ownership fix:
- `proposal.md`: in Impact, drop "needs that change's password settings", and list the password-change lock as this change's own work.
- `design.md`: Decision 4 defines the term and says this change turns the lock on.
- `tasks.md`: in the header, drop the password settings from the dependency list. Task 1.5 becomes "Turn on the password-change lock".
- `specs/agent-read-access/spec.md`: the requirement wording clarifies that the threat is a token holder.

**Supabase Auth acts on the space account, not on a database role.** The database role doesn't cover Auth requests. Two things follow:

- **Replacing the space login.** With only its session token, a handed-over session could ask Supabase Auth to set a new space login. That would lock out every plugin, and let the holder sign in again with sessions that aren't registered and can write. This change turns on the **space login lock**: the Supabase Auth settings `secure_password_change` and "require current password". Together they refuse any change that doesn't supply the current space login, which the holder never has.
- **Signing out the plugins.** A session could sign out the plugins' sessions. That's disruptive but not an escalation, because the plugins sign back in.

content.text:
I've applied the new terms consistently across all six files, and `openspec validate --strict` still passes.

**Terms (each defined once in the design)**
- **Space login:** the credential plugins use to sign in as the space account. Decision 3's context says there are no personal user accounts yet.
- **Session token:** the session's short-lived token, the one the API and the MCP send. Decision 3 separates it from the **refresh token**. That distinction still matters, because the bundle carries only the refresh token and it rotates on every use.
- **Space login lock:** the Supabase Auth setting that stops a holder of a session token from replacing the space login. It's defined in Decision 4.

I didn't use your `api/session_token` or `api/mcp/login` names. They read like route paths, and no such routes exist in the spec. Tell me if you meant them as literal identifiers.

**Ownership:** this change now turns on the space login lock itself, in task 1.5 and migration step 2. The handoff spec is only a dependency for the handoff, the registry and the connect command.

**Renamed requirement:** "Handed-over sessions cannot replace the space login". The scenario is about a token holder asking Supabase Auth for a new space login.

"Password" still appears in Supabase's own names: `signInWithPassword`, `secure_password_change` and the "require current password" setting. "Access token" still appears in "custom access token hook", which is Supabase's feature name. Renaming those would make the spec point at things that don't exist.

"""Convert an OpenSpec markdown file into a Roam bullet tree matching the v2 copy's style."""
import re
import sys

ROOT = "/Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph/openspec/changes/headless-mcp-retrieval/"


class Node:
    def __init__(self, text, heading=0):
        self.text, self.heading, self.children = text, heading, []


def clean(s):
    s = re.sub(r"\s*<!--.*?-->", "", s)
    return s.strip()


def table_node(rows):
    cells = [[c.strip() for c in r.strip().strip("|").split("|")] for r in rows]
    cells = [r for r in cells if not all(re.fullmatch(r"-+", c) for c in r)]
    t = Node("{{[[table]]}}")
    for r in cells:
        cur = Node(r[0])
        t.children.append(cur)
        for c in r[1:]:
            n = Node(c)
            cur.children.append(n)
            cur = n
    return t


def convert(text, levels):
    """levels maps markdown heading depth -> (roam heading level, or 'scenario')."""
    root = Node("")
    stack = [(0, root)]  # (md depth, node)
    lines = text.split("\n")
    i = 0
    last_para = None  # paragraph that a following list may attach to
    list_stack = []  # (indent, node)

    def section():
        return stack[-1][1]

    while i < len(lines):
        line = lines[i]
        m = re.match(r"^(#+)\s+(.*)$", line)
        if m:
            depth = len(m.group(1))
            title = clean(m.group(2))
            list_stack.clear()
            last_para = None
            if depth == 1:
                i += 1
                continue
            while stack and stack[-1][0] >= depth:
                stack.pop()
            kind = levels.get(depth, 0)
            if kind == "scenario":
                n = Node(f"**{title}**")
            else:
                n = Node(title, kind)
            section().children.append(n)
            stack.append((depth, n))
            i += 1
            continue
        if line.startswith("```"):
            block = []
            i += 1
            while not lines[i].startswith("```"):
                block.append(lines[i])
                i += 1
            i += 1
            n = Node("DIAGRAM_PLACEHOLDER")
            n.code = "```plain text\n" + "\n".join(block) + "\n```"
            section().children.append(n)
            last_para = None
            list_stack.clear()
            continue
        if line.startswith("|"):
            rows = []
            while i < len(lines) and lines[i].startswith("|"):
                rows.append(lines[i])
                i += 1
            section().children.append(table_node(rows))
            last_para = None
            list_stack.clear()
            continue
        lm = re.match(r"^(\s*)(?:[-*]|(\d+)\.)\s+(.*)$", line)
        if lm:
            indent = len(lm.group(1))
            body = lm.group(3)
            if lm.group(2):
                body = f"{lm.group(2)}. {body}"
            body = re.sub(r"^\[ \]\s+", "{{[[TODO]]}} ", body)
            n = Node(clean(body))
            while list_stack and list_stack[-1][0] >= indent:
                list_stack.pop()
            if list_stack:
                parent = list_stack[-1][1]
            elif last_para is not None:
                parent = last_para
            else:
                parent = section()
            parent.children.append(n)
            list_stack.append((indent, n))
            i += 1
            continue
        if line.strip() == "":
            i += 1
            continue
        # paragraph (possibly indented continuation under a list item)
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        para = [line.strip()]
        i += 1
        while i < len(lines) and lines[i].strip() and not re.match(r"^\s*(#|[-*] |\d+\. |\||```)", lines[i]):
            para.append(lines[i].strip())
            i += 1
        n = Node(clean(" ".join(para)))
        if indent > 0 and list_stack:
            while list_stack and list_stack[-1][0] >= indent:
                list_stack.pop()
            target = list_stack[-1][1] if list_stack else section()
            target.children.append(n)
            # a list after an indented paragraph nests under it
            list_stack.append((indent - 1, n))
            continue
        section().children.append(n)
        list_stack.clear()
        last_para = n if (n.text.endswith(":") or re.fullmatch(r"\*\*[^*]+\*\*", n.text)) else None
    return root


def render(node, depth=0):
    out = []
    for c in node.children:
        h = "#" * c.heading + " " if c.heading else ""
        out.append("  " * depth + "- " + h + c.text)
        out.extend(render(c, depth + 1))
    return out


DOC_LEVELS = {2: 2, 3: 3}
SPEC_LEVELS = {2: 2, 3: 3, 4: "scenario"}

if __name__ == "__main__":
    which = sys.argv[1]
    if which == "specs":
        top = Node("specs")
        for name in ["headless-retrieval-api", "discourse-retrieval", "agent-read-access", "discourse-mcp"]:
            t = convert(open(f"{ROOT}specs/{name}/spec.md").read(), SPEC_LEVELS)
            sn = Node(f"`{name}`", 1)
            sn.children = t.children
            top.children.append(sn)
        print("- specs")
        print("\n".join(render(top, 1)))
    else:
        title = {"proposal": "Proposal", "design": "Design", "tasks": "Tasks"}[which]
        t = convert(open(f"{ROOT}{which}.md").read(), DOC_LEVELS)
        if which == "proposal":
            t.children = [c for c in t.children if not c.text.startswith("Supersedes")]
        print(f"- # {title}")
        print("\n".join(render(t, 1)))

- # Proposal
  - ## Why
    - Users want to retrieve relevant synced discourse nodes from their agent, or from their own code, without opening Roam or Obsidian. They shouldn't need a separate integration for each platform. This v0 ships a retrieval API, and a local MCP that exposes that API to agent clients. Both use a read-only session of the space account, handed over by the plugin.
  - ## What Changes
    - **A retrieval API** at `/api/v1` in `apps/website`, with four read-only operations: get a node, search nodes, list node types, and get discourse context.
      - It is the one retrieval service: documented for developers, and the only backend of the MCP.
      - It accepts only handed-over sessions.
    - **A local MCP** that exposes each API operation as a tool. Users install it from npm, and the agent client launches it. Supported clients: Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex.
    - **Identity follows Option A2**, decided at the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product meeting. The caller holds its own session of the space account, handed over through `mcp-session-access`, and the database makes that session read-only.
    - **Coverage.** Retrieval covers every synced discourse node the space account can read under its current access. That includes shared nodes that were never imported into the client.
    - **Node shape.** Nodes are `DbCrossAppNode`s identified by `rid`. They reuse discovery's converters and its `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope. Node types are identified by type `rid`.
    - **Search** reuses the stored embeddings through one new search RPC, with type filtering and no relevance cutoff. The API embeds queries on the server.
  - ## Capabilities
    - ### New Capabilities
      - `headless-retrieval-api`: the retrieval service. It provides the four operations over HTTP, accepts only handed-over sessions, and keeps a versioned contract.
      - `discourse-retrieval`: the behavior of those operations: node payloads, semantic search, type discovery and one-hop discourse context.
      - `agent-read-access`: the handed-over session as principal, its current read access, and database-enforced read-only.
      - `discourse-mcp`: the local MCP as a client of the API. Covers tool mapping, session handling, distribution and setup, and the supported clients.
    - ### Modified Capabilities
      - None. The repository has no OpenSpec capability specs yet.
  - ## Out of scope for v0
    - A hosted MCP and ChatGPT support. ChatGPT can't launch a local MCP; a hosted MCP can later wrap the same API.
    - A separate agent principal (Option B).
    - Writes, candidate nodes, non-discourse content, canvas functions, and attachment contents.
    - Multi-hop traversal, keyword or hybrid search, re-embedding, pagination, relevance thresholds, and imported-only filtering.
    - One session that spans several spaces.
  - ## Impact
    - **`packages/database`:**
      - the `mcp_reader` role;
      - a custom access token hook;
      - an `EXECUTE` allowlist for functions;
      - the space login lock;
      - retrieval functions built on the CrossApp converters;
      - one search RPC.
    - **`apps/website`:** the four API routes and their documentation.
    - **A new MCP package** (`apps/mcp`, location proposed), published to npm.
    - **Hosted Supabase settings:** the access token hook, and the space login lock (design Decision 4).
    - **Depends on `mcp-session-access`** (Roam page `Spec: MCP token handoff`) for the handoff, the `mcp_session` registry and sign-out.
    - **Builds on ENG-1985 and ENG-2091** (merged): `dbNodeToCrossApp`, `getSharedNodeByRid` and `SharedNodeListing`.
  - ## Open decisions
    - Whether one agent should span several spaces.
    - Michael hasn't confirmed reusing `CrossAppNode` and `rid` for the agent API (Roam block `SRa9xHk30`).
    - No relevance or latency target is agreed, and the real-query evaluation set doesn't exist yet.

- # Proposal
  - ## Why
    - Users want to retrieve relevant synced discourse nodes from their agent, or from their own code, without opening Roam or Obsidian. They shouldn't need a separate integration for each platform. This v0 ships a retrieval API, and a local MCP that exposes that API to agent clients. Both use a read-only session of the space account, handed over by the plugin.
  - ## What Changes
    - **A retrieval API** at `/api/v1` in `apps/website`, with four read-only operations: get a node, search nodes, list node types, and get discourse context.
      - It is the one retrieval service: documented for developers, and the only backend of the MCP.
      - It accepts only handed-over sessions.
    - **A local MCP** that exposes each API operation as a tool. Users install it from npm, and the agent client launches it. Supported clients: Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex.
    - **Identity follows Option A2**, decided at the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product meeting. The caller holds its own session of the space account, handed over through `mcp-session-access`, and the database makes that session read-only.
    - **Coverage.** Retrieval covers every synced discourse node the space account can read under its current access. That includes shared nodes that were never imported into the client.
    - **Node shape.** Nodes are `DbCrossAppNode`s identified by `rid`. They reuse discovery's converters and its `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope. Node types are identified by type `rid`.
    - **Search** reuses the stored embeddings through one new search RPC, with type filtering and no relevance cutoff. The API embeds queries on the server.
  - ## Capabilities
    - ### New Capabilities
      - `headless-retrieval-api`: the retrieval service. It provides the four operations over HTTP, accepts only handed-over sessions, and keeps a versioned contract.
      - `discourse-retrieval`: the behavior of those operations: node payloads, semantic search, type discovery and one-hop discourse context.
      - `agent-read-access`: the handed-over session as principal, its current read access, and database-enforced read-only.
      - `discourse-mcp`: the local MCP as a client of the API. Covers tool mapping, session handling, distribution and setup, and the supported clients.
    - ### Modified Capabilities
      - None. The repository has no OpenSpec capability specs yet.
  - ## Out of scope for v0
    - A hosted MCP and ChatGPT support. ChatGPT can't launch a local MCP; a hosted MCP can later wrap the same API.
    - A separate agent principal (Option B).
    - Writes, candidate nodes, non-discourse content, canvas functions, and attachment contents.
    - Multi-hop traversal, keyword or hybrid search, re-embedding, pagination, relevance thresholds, and imported-only filtering.
    - One session that spans several spaces.
  - ## Impact
    - **`packages/database`:**
      - the `mcp_reader` role;
      - a custom access token hook;
      - an `EXECUTE` allowlist for functions;
      - the space login lock;
      - retrieval functions built on the CrossApp converters;
      - one search RPC.
    - **`apps/website`:** the four API routes and their documentation.
    - **A new MCP package** (`apps/mcp`, location proposed), published to npm.
    - **Hosted Supabase settings:** the access token hook, and the space login lock (design Decision 4).
    - **Depends on `mcp-session-access`** ([[Spec: MCP token handoff]]) for the handoff, the `mcp_session` registry and sign-out.
    - **Builds on ENG-1985 and ENG-2091** (merged): `dbNodeToCrossApp`, `getSharedNodeByRid` and `SharedNodeListing`.
  - ## Open decisions
    - Whether one agent should span several spaces.
    - Michael hasn't confirmed reusing `CrossAppNode` and `rid` for the agent API (((SRa9xHk30))).
    - No relevance or latency target is agreed, and the real-query evaluation set doesn't exist yet.

- # Design
  - ## Context
    - These facts from `origin/main` shape the design.
    - **Identity and data**
      - **Space accounts.** Plugins sign in as a per-space account with `signInWithPassword` (`packages/database/src/lib/contextFunctions.ts`). This spec calls that credential the **space login**. It's a random secret stored in the plugin; there are no personal user accounts yet. `mcp-session-access` adds the handoff and the `mcp_session` registry; none of it is in the repo yet.
      - **Concepts and content.** `Concept` holds node instances, schemas and relations (`is_schema`, `is_relation`). `Content` joins it on `(space_id, source_local_id)`, with variants `direct`, `direct_and_children`, `direct_and_description` and `full`.
      - **Readability.** The `my_*` views, and helpers such as `in_space` and `can_view_specific_resource`, express what a caller can read.
    - **Discovery and embeddings**
      - **Discovery (ENG-2091).** `packages/database/src/lib/sharedNodes.ts` returns a `SharedNodeListing`, which is `{ nodes, spaces }` of `DbCrossAppNode`.
        - `getSharedNodeByRid` reads one readable node by `rid`.
        - `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` converts nodes, node schemas and relations.
        - Neither the listing nor the converter includes `content.full`; import fetches it separately.
      - **Embeddings.** `embedding.sql` stores 1536-dimension `text-embedding-3-small` vectors with an `obsolete` flag.
        - `match_content_embeddings` applies a similarity threshold and has no type filter.
        - Obsidian embeds the title (`direct`).
        - Roam embeds `direct_and_description` when a node has a description, and `direct` otherwise.
        - The website embeds text with the team's OpenAI key (`/api/embeddings/openai/small`).
    - **Database access controls**
      - **Row-level security.** 61 of the 65 policies have no `TO` clause. The other four are `TO authenticated` on `storage.objects`, which retrieval does not read. Table grants go only to `authenticated` and `service_role`.
      - **Function privileges.** `PUBLIC` can execute every function in `public`, because no schema file revokes the default. Some write functions are `SECURITY DEFINER`, such as `create_secret_token` and `accept_group_invitation`, so table grants alone don't stop them.
      - **Auth settings.** `config.toml` sets `jwt_expiry = 3600` and leaves the custom access token hook commented out.
  - ## Goals / Non-Goals
    - **Goals:**
      - One retrieval service. Every client, the MCP included, goes through the API.
      - Reuse existing data, vectors, converters and access rules.
      - The database, not the API or the MCP, enforces read-only.
      - Sync gaps are reported as errors, never as partial content.
    - **Non-Goals:**
      - A new identity system.
      - A hosted MCP.
      - A second embedding pipeline.
      - Attachment access.
      - Auditing.
  - ## Decisions
    - ### 1. The API is the retrieval service; the MCP is its client
      - DIAGRAM_PLACEHOLDER
      - The API holds all retrieval logic.
      - **Routes.** It's four routes in `apps/website` that call `packages/database` functions with the caller's session, so row-level security applies.
      - **MCP.** The MCP holds a session and maps each tool to one API call. It never reads the database or calls OpenAI.
      - **Developers** call the same routes directly.
      - **The contract is `/api/v1`.** Installed MCP copies can't be force-updated, so `/api/v1` changes only additively, and a breaking change needs `/api/v2`. Schema, query and converter fixes behind the API ship by deploying the website, without an MCP release.
      - **Alternatives:**
        - **The MCP reads the database directly.**
          - Installed copies would then depend on the view shapes, and fixes would need an MCP release.
          - The MCP would bundle database code and call an embedding route outside the API's auth.
          - The API and the MCP would be two adapters to keep in parity.
        - **A hosted MCP in `apps/website` (the 2026-09-25 version).** It reaches ChatGPT, but it needs a hosted credential store. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose a local MCP. A hosted MCP can still wrap this API later.
    - ### 2. Reuse the discovery read path
      - The API's routes call TypeScript functions in `packages/database` that build on Sid's discovery code:
        - **Get-node** calls `getSharedNodeByRid`, then fetches the `full` Content the way import does.
        - **Type discovery** reads node types from readable node instances and labels them with `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp`.
        - **Discourse context** reads the readable relation instances whose `refs` contain the node. It takes direction from the `source` and `destination` keys of `reference_content`, and converts the relations with `dbRelationsToCrossApp`.
      - Only search needs a new RPC (Decision 6).
      - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** four new `SECURITY INVOKER` RPCs. They duplicate the converters.
    - ### 3. Hand over a session through `mcp-session-access`
      - `mcp-session-access` defines the handoff.
      - **Handoff.**
        - 1. The plugin opens a new session for the space account, using a second client that neither persists nor auto-refreshes.
        - 2. It registers the session with `register_mcp_session(label)`.
        - 3. It shows the bundle once: Supabase URL, anon key, space ID and refresh token. It keeps no copy.
      - **Registry.** `mcp_session` records the session ID (from the caller's own token), the label, the space account and the creation time.
      - **Sign-out.** The holder can sign itself out with local scope. Per-session sign-out from the plugin is proposed for right after v0.
      - **Emergency switch.** Until then, the cut-off is to sign out every other session of the space account. That also signs out the other plugin instances, which sign back in with the space login.
      - **Who can connect.** Any plugin user of the space.
      - **Tokens.** Two tokens are involved:
        - the **session token** is the session's short-lived access token, the one the API takes;
        - the **refresh token** renews the session token, and it rotates on every use.
      - The bundle carries only the refresh token, so the holder's first session token comes from a refresh and already carries `mcp_reader` (Decision 4). The plugin discards the `authenticated` session token it used to register.
      - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** a separate Supabase auth user for each agent grant (Option B), with an opaque credential issued from a website page. The 2026-11-10 meeting judged its security gain marginal for the extra work.
    - ### 4. The database makes handed-over sessions read-only (A2)
      - The session token also works against Supabase directly, outside the API. So the database, not the API, enforces read-only.
      - **The hook.** A custom access token hook runs on every token issue and refresh. When the token's `session_id` is in `mcp_session`, it sets the `role` claim to `mcp_reader` (name proposed). Other sessions keep `authenticated`.
      - **The role.** `mcp_reader`:
        - is granted to `authenticator`, so PostgREST can switch to it;
        - has `SELECT` on the tables and views retrieval reads, and no `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`;
        - has `EXECUTE` on an allowlist: the search RPC, and the access helpers that the policies and views call.
      - **Locking down functions.** Because `PUBLIC` holds `EXECUTE` on every function, the allowlist needs two changes:
        - `REVOKE EXECUTE ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC`;
        - the matching default-privilege change.
      - `anon` and `authenticated` keep their explicit grants. A test lists every function `mcp_reader` can execute and compares the list with the allowlist. Policies without a `TO` clause cover `mcp_reader`, so reads follow the space account's current access.
      - **Supabase Auth acts on the space account, not on a database role.** The database role doesn't cover Auth requests. Two things follow:
        - **Replacing the space login.** With only its session token, a handed-over session could ask Supabase Auth to set a new space login. That would lock out every plugin, and let the holder sign in again with sessions that aren't registered and can write. This change turns on the **space login lock**: the Supabase Auth settings `secure_password_change` and "require current password". Together they refuse any change that doesn't supply the current space login, which the holder never has.
        - **Signing out the plugins.** A session could sign out the plugins' sessions. That's disruptive but not an escalation, because the plugins sign back in.
      - **A switched-off hook fails open.** Handed-over sessions would then get `authenticated`. Two checks catch a misconfigured project:
        - the API rejects any token whose `role` isn't `mcp_reader`;
        - the MCP refuses to start unless its session token carries `mcp_reader`.
      - **Revocation waits for token expiry.** Sign-out stops refresh, but the current session token stays valid for up to `jwt_expiry` (3600 s). The 2026-11-10 meeting accepted this.
      - **Alternative: plain A**, where only the tools are read-only. Any process holding the bundle could write. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose A2 because the threat is overeager agent harnesses that bypass the MCP.
    - ### 5. Nodes are CrossApp nodes, identified by `rid`
      - **Identifiers**
        - **Nodes.** A node's ID is its `rid`, built by `spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid`.
          - For an `http` space URI it's `<space URI>/<localId>`. Otherwise it's `orn:<platform>.note:…/<localId>`.
          - Look nodes up by space and `localId`, never by `localId` alone.
        - **Types.** A type's ID is its `rid` (`getNodeTypeRid`), never the space-relative `nodeType`. Type filters take type `rid`s, and same-named types in different spaces stay separate.
      - **Payload**
        - **Envelope.** Each operation returns `DbCrossAppNode`s in discovery's `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope.
        - **Added fields.** Each node gets a `typeRid`; search also adds a `score` and an `excerpt`. There's no separate agent node type.
        - **Title and body.** The title is `content.direct`. Get-node adds `content.full` as stored text or markdown, never rendered HTML.
        - **Links and assets.** Source links stay as text. Assets aren't fetched, and no storage URLs are minted.
        - **Provenance.** It's the `rid` plus its `spaces` entry. Nothing implies the node exists in the caller's vault.
      - **Gaps are errors**
        - **Listings and search** skip rows the converter can't convert, as discovery does.
        - **Get-node doesn't skip:**
          - `getSharedNodeByRid` returns `null` for a missing or unreadable node, which maps to `not_found`;
          - a conversion failure or a missing `full` Content maps to `content_unavailable`.
        - A stored empty body is not a missing row.
      - **Alternative (2026-09-25 version):** an agent-specific payload keyed by `Concept.id`, which no plugin uses. It would give each node a second identity.
    - ### 6. Search reuses stored vectors through one new RPC
      - The API embeds the query on the server with `text-embedding-3-small` at 1536 dimensions, using the OpenAI client that `/api/embeddings/openai/small` builds inline today, extracted into a shared helper. Embedding happens only after the API has authenticated the caller. Neither the MCP nor a developer calls the embedding route.
      - The new `SECURITY INVOKER` RPC takes a vector, optional type `rid`s and a limit. It:
        - joins the current, non-obsolete `direct` and `direct_and_description` embeddings of readable node instances;
        - keeps each node's best similarity, once;
        - applies authorization, type filter and deduplication before the limit;
        - sorts by similarity, then `rid`;
        - has no similarity threshold, so negative similarities stay eligible.
      - **Other behavior**
        - `match_content_embeddings` stays unchanged.
        - Nodes without a usable embedding are absent from search, but the other operations still reach them.
        - Embedding failures are errors, not empty results.

      - **Concepts and content.** `Concept` holds node instances, schemas and relations (`is_schema`, `is_relation`). `Content` joins it on `(space_id, source_local_id)`, with variants `direct`, `direct_and_children`, `direct_and_description` and `full`.

    - **Discovery and embeddings**
      - **Discovery (ENG-2091).** `packages/database/src/lib/sharedNodes.ts` returns a `SharedNodeListing`, which is `{ nodes, spaces }` of `DbCrossAppNode`.
        - `getSharedNodeByRid` reads one readable node by `rid`.
        - `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` converts nodes, node schemas and relations.
        - Neither the listing nor the converter includes `content.full`; import fetches it separately.
      - **Embeddings.** `embedding.sql` stores 1536-dimension `text-embedding-3-small` vectors with an `obsolete` flag.
        - `match_content_embeddings` applies a similarity threshold and has no type filter.
        - Obsidian embeds the title (`direct`).
        - Roam embeds `direct_and_description` when a node has a description, and `direct` otherwise.
        - The website embeds text with the team's OpenAI key (`/api/embeddings/openai/small`).
    - **Database access controls**
      - **Row-level security.** 61 of the 65 policies have no `TO` clause. The other four are `TO authenticated` on `storage.objects`, which retrieval does not read. Table grants go only to `authenticated` and `service_role`.
      - **Function privileges.** `PUBLIC` can execute every function in `public`, because no schema file revokes the default. Some write functions are `SECURITY DEFINER`, such as `create_secret_token` and `accept_group_invitation`, so table grants alone don't stop them.

    - **Goals:**
      - One retrieval service. Every client, the MCP included, goes through the API.
      - Reuse existing data, vectors, converters and access rules.
      - The database, not the API or the MCP, enforces read-only.
      - Sync gaps are reported as errors, never as partial content.

      - A new identity system.
      - A hosted MCP.
      - A second embedding pipeline.
      - Attachment access.
      - Auditing.

      - **Alternatives:**
        - **The MCP reads the database directly.**
          - Installed copies would then depend on the view shapes, and fixes would need an MCP release.
          - The MCP would bundle database code and call an embedding route outside the API's auth.
          - The API and the MCP would be two adapters to keep in parity.
        - **A hosted MCP in `apps/website` (the 2026-09-25 version).** It reaches ChatGPT, but it needs a hosted credential store. The 2026-11-10 meeting chose a local MCP. A hosted MCP can still wrap this API later.
    - ### 2. Reuse the discovery read path
      - The API's routes call TypeScript functions in `packages/database` that build on Sid's discovery code:
        - **Get-node** calls `getSharedNodeByRid`, then fetches the `full` Content the way import does.

  - # `headless-retrieval-api`
    - ## Purpose
      - Provide the retrieval service: four read-only operations over HTTP, which developers call directly and the MCP calls on behalf of agent clients.
    - ## ADDED Requirements
      - ### Requirement: Four retrieval operations
        - The system SHALL provide an HTTP API for get-node, search-nodes, discover-node-types and get-discourse-context. These operations SHALL follow the `discourse-retrieval` and `agent-read-access` contracts. The API SHALL be the only retrieval backend for the MCP.
        - **Scenario: Developer calls each operation directly**
          - **WHEN** a developer calls each of the four operations with a valid handed-over session
          - **THEN** each operation applies the shared retrieval and authorization rules
          - **AND** no MCP is required
      - ### Requirement: Response envelope
        - Every API response SHALL carry a request ID. It SHALL also carry either `data` or an error object with a stable code and a safe message. An error SHALL NOT be returned as an empty `data` collection.
        - **Scenario: Failed request**
          - **WHEN** an operation fails
          - **THEN** the response has a request ID and an error object with a stable code and a message that doesn't expose internals
          - **AND** the response has no `data`
      - ### Requirement: Handed-over sessions only
        - The API SHALL accept only a session token from a handed-over session, which carries the read-only database role. It SHALL reject missing, invalid and expired tokens, and tokens from any other session, including plugin sessions. It SHALL NOT store tokens between requests.
        - **Scenario: Plugin session token**
          - **WHEN** a request carries a valid session token from a plugin's own session
          - **THEN** the API rejects it, and returns no discourse data
        - **Scenario: Missing or expired token**
          - **WHEN** a request carries no token, or an expired one
          - **THEN** the API rejects it as unauthenticated
      - ### Requirement: Versioned contract
        - The API SHALL serve its operations under a version prefix. Changes within a version SHALL be additive. A breaking change SHALL ship under a new version, alongside the old one.
        - **Scenario: An installed MCP after a server change**
          - **GIVEN** an installed MCP built against `/api/v1`
          - **WHEN** the website deploys a change within `/api/v1`
          - **THEN** the installed MCP's requests keep working
      - ### Requirement: Documented developer contract
        - The API documentation SHALL cover:
          - authentication, including how to get a token;
          - inputs and outputs;
          - errors;
          - search limits;
          - type-filter semantics;
          - the per-space access model.
        - It SHALL also explain that:
          - readable unimported nodes can appear;
          - the existing embeddings determine semantic coverage;
          - search can return weak matches;
          - v0 search has no pagination.
        - **Scenario: Set up a direct integration**
          - **WHEN** a developer follows the API documentation with a handed-over session
          - **THEN** the documentation gives a working example for each of the four operations, and explains their results and errors
      - ### Requirement: Headless retrieval after setup
        - After handoff and sync, the API SHALL work without Roam or Obsidian open. Responses SHALL come from the database's synced state.
        - **Scenario: Source application is closed**
          - **GIVEN** a user has synced nodes and a handed-over session
          - **WHEN** Roam and Obsidian are closed, and a caller calls the API
          - **THEN** eligible synced data is returned
  - # `discourse-retrieval`
    - ## Purpose
      - Let agents retrieve synced discourse node text, search by meaning with the existing embeddings, discover node types, and follow explicit one-hop discourse context, all within current read access.
    - ## ADDED Requirements
      - ### Requirement: Readable synced collection
        - All retrieval operations SHALL use already-synced discourse data readable by the handed-over space account. Local import status and authorship SHALL NOT restrict that collection. Results MUST NOT imply that the returned nodes were imported into the client application.
        - **Scenario: Readable but unimported node**
          - **GIVEN** a synced discourse node is readable by the principal, but was authored elsewhere and never imported into its client
          - **WHEN** the agent fetches it or searches for it
          - **THEN** the node is eligible for retrieval and search ranking
          - **AND** the response does not claim the node was imported locally
        - **Scenario: Unreadable node**
          - **WHEN** an agent requests a node that its principal cannot read
          - **THEN** retrieval returns neither the node's content nor its metadata
      - ### Requirement: Nodes and types are identified by rid
        - Every operation SHALL identify a node by its `rid` and a node type by the type's `rid`. Type filters SHALL take type `rid`s. Types with the same name in different spaces SHALL stay separate.
        - **Scenario: Same-named types in two spaces**
          - **GIVEN** two readable spaces each define a type named "Claim"
          - **WHEN** the agent discovers node types
          - **THEN** it sees two types with different `rid`s
      - ### Requirement: Full node text
        - Getting a readable node SHALL return its `rid`, title, type `rid`, full synced text body, and provenance. The body SHALL be the stored synced text, not content fetched live from the client application. Attachment downloads and file contents SHALL stay outside this operation.
        - **Scenario: Get a node with body text and attachment links**
          - **WHEN** an agent fetches a readable synced node whose text links to an attachment
          - **THEN** it receives the required node fields and the full stored text, including the source links in that text
          - **AND** the response doesn't download or embed the attachment's file contents
      - ### Requirement: Existing semantic search
        - Search SHALL reuse the stored embeddings, including Roam's title-plus-description embeddings, and SHALL NOT require re-embedding. Matching SHALL reflect the existing embedding inputs; it doesn't promise full-body coverage. V0 SHALL NOT require keyword matching or hybrid ranking. Each result SHALL contain the node's `rid`, title, type `rid`, a short excerpt and provenance, ordered by relevance.
        - **Scenario: Semantic search results**
          - **WHEN** an agent submits a query, and eligible nodes have current embeddings
          - **THEN** results are ranked by semantic similarity and include the required fields
          - **AND** no node is excluded only because its title lacks the query's exact words
        - **Scenario: Existing title-plus-description embedding**
          - **GIVEN** a readable Roam node has an embedding generated from its title and description
          - **WHEN** the agent searches
          - **THEN** that embedding contributes to ranking
        - **Scenario: Unembedded body changes**
          - **GIVEN** embeddings, permissions and filters are unchanged
          - **WHEN** only a node's full synced body changes
          - **THEN** its semantic matching score doesn't change
      - ### Requirement: Bounded search without a relevance cutoff
        - Search SHALL default to 10 results and accept a limit from 1 to 30. A limit outside that range SHALL be rejected. V0 SHALL NOT paginate. It SHALL NOT discard eligible nodes because their relevance is low. An empty result SHALL mean that no searchable nodes meet the access and type constraints.
        - **Scenario: Default and explicit limits**
          - **GIVEN** at least 30 eligible searchable nodes
          - **WHEN** the agent searches without a limit, and then with a limit of 20
          - **THEN** the responses contain 10 and 20 results
          - **AND** neither response offers a continuation page
        - **Scenario: Weak matches**
          - **GIVEN** three eligible searchable nodes with weak similarity, and a limit of 10
          - **WHEN** the agent searches
          - **THEN** all three are returned in relevance order
        - **Scenario: Limit above the maximum**
          - **WHEN** a request asks for more than 30 results
          - **THEN** it is rejected as an invalid request
        - **Scenario: Empty eligible collection**
          - **WHEN** no searchable nodes meet the principal's access and type constraints
          - **THEN** search returns an empty result
      - ### Requirement: Readable type discovery and filtering
        - Type discovery SHALL return type `rid`s and names only for types present on nodes the principal can currently read, including shared nodes. Search SHALL accept one or more type `rid`s and match any of them. Without a filter, search SHALL cover all eligible types.
        - **Scenario: Discover types from readable nodes**
          - **GIVEN** type A is on a readable shared node, and type B is only on unreadable nodes
          - **WHEN** the agent discovers node types
          - **THEN** type A is listed and type B is not
        - **Scenario: Multiple selected types**
          - **WHEN** the agent searches with types A and B selected
          - **THEN** every result has type A or B and is readable by the principal
        - **Scenario: No type filter**
          - **WHEN** the agent searches without a type filter
          - **THEN** no eligible node is excluded because of its type
      - ### Requirement: One-hop discourse context
        - Discourse context SHALL return the incoming and outgoing explicit discourse relationships of a readable node. Each relationship SHALL give its type, its direction relative to the requested node, and the connected node's `rid`, title and type `rid`. Both endpoints MUST be readable. Ordinary backlinks SHALL be excluded. Connected bodies SHALL be retrieved separately through get-node. A single call SHALL NOT traverse past one hop.
        - **Scenario: Incoming and outgoing relationships**
          - **GIVEN** readable nodes A and B have an explicit relationship from A to B
          - **WHEN** the agent requests discourse context for A, and then for B
          - **THEN** the relationship is outgoing for A and incoming for B, each with the connected node's summary
        - **Scenario: Inaccessible endpoint and ordinary backlink**
          - **GIVEN** readable node A has an explicit relationship to unreadable node B, and an ordinary backlink from readable node C
          - **WHEN** the agent requests A's discourse context
          - **THEN** neither the relationship to B nor the backlink from C is returned
        - **Scenario: Repeated one-hop calls**
          - **GIVEN** readable nodes A, B and C have relationships A to B and B to C, and none from A to C
          - **WHEN** the agent requests A's discourse context
          - **THEN** the call doesn't traverse B to return C
          - **AND** a later request for B's discourse context returns the relationship to C
  - # `agent-read-access`
    - ## Purpose
      - Let an agent read a space's synced discourse graph through its own read-only session of the space account.
    - ## ADDED Requirements
      - ### Requirement: Session handed over through `mcp-session-access`
        - The MCP SHALL use a session that a plugin handed over and registered through `mcp-session-access`. No website session or agent-management page SHALL be required. The MCP SHALL NOT receive the space login.
        - **Scenario: Connect from either platform**
          - **WHEN** a user runs the connect command in a signed-in Roam or Obsidian client
          - **THEN** the plugin shows a bundle for a new, registered session of that client's space account
          - **AND** the plugin's own session is unchanged
      - ### Requirement: Per-space principal
        - The system SHALL treat the space account whose session was handed over as the principal. Retrieval SHALL use that account's readable collection. It SHALL NOT combine the access of other space accounts that the same person uses. Reading another space's synced but unpublished nodes SHALL require a bundle from that space.
        - **Scenario: Another space's private synced nodes**
          - **GIVEN** a person uses spaces A and B, and a node in B is not readable by A's space account
          - **WHEN** an agent uses a bundle from space A
          - **THEN** it cannot retrieve the node in B
        - **Scenario: Accessible shared node**
          - **GIVEN** a node from another space is readable by the space account through sharing
          - **WHEN** the agent retrieves that node
          - **THEN** the node is returned, even though the space account didn't import or author it
      - ### Requirement: Current permissions
        - The system SHALL evaluate retrieval against the space account's current read permissions. Removing access SHALL stop later retrieval of the affected data. Adding access SHALL make the affected synced data eligible. Neither SHALL require a new bundle.
        - **Scenario: Permissions change after handoff**
          - **WHEN** a space account gains access to node A and loses access to node B after a bundle is handed over
          - **THEN** later requests with that bundle can retrieve A and cannot retrieve B
      - ### Requirement: Session sign-out
        - The MCP SHALL be able to sign its own session out. A signed-out session SHALL NOT refresh. A session token it already holds MAY stay valid until it expires.
        - **Scenario: Signed-out session**
          - **WHEN** a handed-over session is signed out
          - **THEN** the MCP cannot refresh it
          - **AND** requests fail once its current session token expires
      - ### Requirement: The database refuses writes from handed-over sessions
        - The database SHALL refuse every create, modify or delete made with a handed-over session, whichever client makes it. That includes calls to write functions. The session SHALL keep the space account's read access. Plugin sessions SHALL keep their permissions. Missing or expired sessions SHALL NOT authorize retrieval.
        - **Scenario: Write made outside the MCP's tools**
          - **GIVEN** a process holds a handed-over session, and the space account can edit a node
          - **WHEN** the process modifies the node or calls a write function directly with that session
          - **THEN** the database refuses it
          - **AND** the node remains unchanged
        - **Scenario: Plugin session keeps write access**
          - **GIVEN** a plugin has handed over a session
          - **WHEN** the plugin writes with its own session
          - **THEN** the write succeeds
        - **Scenario: Unauthenticated retrieval**
          - **WHEN** a retrieval request has a missing or expired session
          - **THEN** no discourse data is returned
      - ### Requirement: Handed-over sessions cannot replace the space login
        - A handed-over session SHALL NOT be able to replace the space login with only its session token.
        - **Scenario: Agent tries to replace the space login**
          - **WHEN** a process asks Supabase Auth to set a new space login, using a handed-over session token
          - **THEN** Supabase Auth refuses the request
          - **AND** the space's plugins still sign in with the existing space login
  - # `discourse-mcp`
    - ## Purpose
      - Expose the retrieval API to agent clients through one local MCP, for both Roam and Obsidian. The MCP runs on the user's machine with a session the plugin hands over.
    - ## ADDED Requirements
      - ### Requirement: Tools are thin clients of the API
        - The MCP SHALL expose tools for get-node, search-nodes, discover-node-types and get-discourse-context, and no other tools. Each tool SHALL call exactly one operation of the retrieval API. It SHALL return that operation's result, and SHALL turn the operation's error into a tool error with the same code. The MCP SHALL NOT read the database or call an embedding service itself.
        - **Scenario: Tool discovery**
          - **WHEN** an agent client lists the MCP's tools
          - **THEN** it sees exactly the four retrieval tools, each with its input definition and a read-only annotation
        - **Scenario: API error**
          - **WHEN** the API returns an error for a tool call
          - **THEN** the tool returns an error with the same code, not an empty result
        - **Scenario: API unreachable**
          - **WHEN** the API can't be reached
          - **THEN** the tool returns a dependency error
        - **Scenario: Agent asks the MCP to modify a node**
          - **WHEN** an agent asks the MCP to modify a node
          - **THEN** no MCP tool can perform the modification
      - ### Requirement: Distribution and setup
        - The MCP SHALL install from npm. It SHALL take the bundle through a connect step that stores the session outside the agent client's configuration. It SHALL persist every rotated refresh token. It SHALL refuse to run a second process for the same connection. It SHALL refuse to start when its session lacks the read-only database role.
        - **Scenario: Connect stores the session locally**
          - **WHEN** a user runs the connect step with a bundle
          - **THEN** the session is stored in a local state file that only the user can read
          - **AND** the agent client's configuration holds no token
        - **Scenario: Restart after a refresh**
          - **GIVEN** the MCP has refreshed its session at least once
          - **WHEN** the agent client restarts the MCP
          - **THEN** the MCP resumes with the latest refresh token
        - **Scenario: Second process for one connection**
          - **WHEN** a second MCP process starts for a connection that is already running
          - **THEN** it exits with a clear error, and does not refresh the session
        - **Scenario: Read-only role missing**
          - **WHEN** the MCP's session token doesn't carry the read-only role
          - **THEN** the MCP refuses to start, and reports a project configuration error
      - ### Requirement: Supported agent clients
        - V0 SHALL document setup for Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex. All four operations SHALL work in each of them, with Roam and Obsidian closed. ChatGPT isn't supported, because it can't launch a local MCP.
        - **Scenario: Validate each client**
          - **GIVEN** synced readable data, and a bundle from the supported handoff
          - **WHEN** setup and tool execution are validated separately in Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex, with Roam and Obsidian closed
          - **THEN** each client launches the MCP and completes all four retrieval operations

content.text:
Here are answers to your four questions, then the edits I'd make. Nothing is written yet.

## 1. "It accepts only handed-over sessions"

**What it means:** the API takes only session tokens from sessions a plugin handed over. Those tokens carry the read-only database role. The API rejects the plugins' own sessions, which can write. That way the website never handles a token that can write.

**Future services:** the real rule is "read-only sessions only". "Handed-over" is just how a read-only session is obtained today. Another service would get its session through the same handoff, or through a later identity such as an agent account (Option B), which would also carry the read-only role. So the rule still applies, but it should be phrased by role, not by how the session was obtained.

**Does it belong in the proposal?** No, it's a detail. Proposed edits:
- **Proposal:** remove the sub-bullet.
- **API spec:** rename the requirement to "Read-only sessions only". The text would be: "The API SHALL accept only session tokens that carry the read-only database role. Today these come from sessions a plugin handed over."

## 2. A2 summary, and explaining code identifiers everywhere

**Proposed A2 sentence:**
> **Identity follows Option A2** ([decision](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/guIcK3Z9M), [options compared](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/bTMUCrCnD)): the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. Decided at the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product meeting.

**Rule for the whole spec** (proposal, design, the four specs and tasks): at each identifier's first use in a file, add a short plain-words gloss, plus a link where a source exists. After the first use, the bare identifier is enough. The glosses I'd use:

| Identifier | Gloss | Link |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mcp-session-access` | session handoff spec | Roam page `Spec: MCP token handoff` |
| `mcp_session` | registry of handed-over sessions | same page |
| `mcp_reader` | read-only database role | design Decision 4 |
| A2 / Option B | (blurb above) / separate agent account | Roam options blocks |
| `rid` | global node ID | ENG-2050 |
| `DbCrossAppNode`, `SharedNodeListing` | shared node format / node listing with spaces | ENG-2091 |
| `getSharedNodeByRid`, `dbNodeToCrossApp`, … | discovery read helper / node converter | ENG-2091, ENG-1985 |
| `match_content_embeddings` | existing semantic search query | none |
| `SECURITY INVOKER` / `DEFINER` | runs as the caller / runs as the owner | none |
| `PUBLIC`, `authenticator` | every database role / the API's login role | none |
| `jwt_expiry` | session token lifetime | none |
| ENG-1985, ENG-2091 | the ticket title, as a Linear link | Linear |
| capability names | a short purpose phrase | none |

## 3. `discourse-retrieval` is unclear

Proposed text:
> `discourse-retrieval`: what the four retrieval operations return, whichever client calls them (the API directly, or the MCP through it). Covers node payloads, semantic search, type discovery and one-hop discourse context.

## 4. Search: what happens today, and keyword search

**Today, search already runs from the API.** The route embeds the query with OpenAI, then makes one database call that ranks stored embeddings by similarity. That ranking has to happen in Postgres, because the vectors live there and the read-access check runs there too. Pulling vectors into the API to rank them would be much heavier, not lighter. The "new RPC" is just that one query.

**Keyword search is lighter, though.** You're right on that point. A plain match on titles needs no OpenAI call and can use the existing views with no new SQL. The deferred piece was *hybrid* search: merging keyword and semantic rankings into one list. That's the complex part. Plain keyword search was only deferred alongside it.

**Two options:**
- **A. Semantic only (current).** One mode, one ranking. Exact-title lookups depend on how well the embeddings match.
- **B. Add `mode: "keyword"`.** It's a case-insensitive title match over readable nodes, with the same type filter and limit, ordered by `rid`.
  - **Cost:** one function plus tests, with no RPC and no embedding call.
  - **Spec impact:** one new requirement in `discourse-retrieval`, an optional `mode` input on search, and the out-of-scope line narrowed to "hybrid ranking".

I lean towards B. It's cheap, and agents often know the exact title they're looking for.

input.ask: Approve these edits across the spec files?

content.text:
## 1. Read-only: yes, it belongs to the MCP's session, not the API

You're right. Read-only is a property of the session handed to an agent (`agent-read-access`, the read-only access spec), and the database enforces it. The API only exposes read operations, so even a session that can write can't write through it. The only reason the API rejected plugin sessions was to keep tokens that can write from passing through the website, and log redaction already covers that.

**Proposed edits:**
- **Proposal:** remove the "accepts only handed-over sessions" sub-bullet.
- **API spec:** replace "Handed-over sessions only" with "**Authenticated sessions**": the API SHALL accept a valid session token for a space account, and reject missing, invalid and expired tokens. The plugin-session scenario goes away.
- **Design Decision 8:** drop the "reject unless `mcp_reader`" step.
  - Decision 4's fail-open check then relies only on the MCP's startup check, which stays.
  - The risk line about tokens passing through the website becomes: "Any space-account session token may pass through; routes only read, and the `Authorization` header stays out of logs."
- **Tasks 4.2:** remove the "plugin session returns 401" case.

**Trade-off:** a leaked plugin token from the website's logs could write for up to an hour. Log redaction is now the only thing preventing that leak, so it's worth weighing against the hosting-log check you chose to leave out.

## 2. Glosses: repeat once per section

Updated rule: gloss an identifier at its first use **in each section**, meaning each heading such as a Decision, Requirement or task group, plus a link the first time in each file. A reader landing on any section then has the context without scrolling back.

## 3. Where `discourse-retrieval` sits

It's a layer below both:

```
agent client --> MCP tools ----+   (transport: tools; passes results through)
                               v
developer ---------------> API routes   (transport: HTTP, auth, envelope, versioning)
                               |           = spec `headless-retrieval-api`
                               v
              retrieval core in packages/database
              (what the 4 operations return)
                               = spec `discourse-retrieval`
```

The MCP passes results through unchanged, so `discourse-retrieval` effectively describes what the **API returns**. The two API-side specs split as "what" (`discourse-retrieval`) and "how you reach it" (`headless-retrieval-api`).

**Proposed descriptions:**
- `discourse-retrieval`: **"What the API's four operations return:** which nodes are eligible, node payloads, semantic search, type discovery and one-hop discourse context."
- `headless-retrieval-api`: **"How callers reach those operations:** HTTP routes, session auth, the response envelope and the versioned contract."
- `discourse-mcp`: **"How agent clients reach the API:** four tools that pass API results through, plus setup and distribution."

I'd add the diagram to design Decision 1 as well.

**Alternative:** merge `discourse-retrieval` into `headless-retrieval-api`, giving one spec for the API. That removes the layering question entirely, but makes that one spec large.

## 4. Search stays semantic only

No change needed.
oh wait for 4. don't supabase have a hybrid search already? we can just use that function?

Close, but not quite. Supabase doesn't ship a hybrid search function you can call. Its docs give a **recipe**: a `hybrid_search` SQL function that you copy into your own schema and adapt. I'm going from memory of the Supabase hybrid search guide and haven't re-checked it today.

**What the recipe assumes**
- A table with a generated `tsvector` full-text column, a GIN index on it, and an embedding column, all in one row.
- One query that ranks by keyword (`websearch_to_tsquery`) and by vector similarity, then merges the two lists with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), using tunable weights.

**What adapting it here would take**
- **Schema:** our text lives in `Content` and the vectors in a separate embeddings table. So we'd add a generated full-text column on `Content`, for example over `direct` and `direct_and_description` text, plus a GIN index. That's one migration, and it doesn't change the plugins.
- **Search RPC:** we're writing a dedicated one anyway (task 3.1). It would fold in the keyword ranking and the RRF merge, on top of the readability check, type filter and per-node deduplication.
- **Contract changes:**
  - `score` becomes a fused rank score, not a cosine similarity.
  - The "negative similarity is still returned" scenario gets rewritten.
  - The API probably exposes the fusion weights as fixed defaults, not inputs.

**Cost:** moderate, not free. It's one more migration and a more complex query plus tests, roughly a day or two on top of task 3. The real benefit is that exact-word queries (names, acronyms, titles) rank well even when the embeddings miss them.

**Options**
- **A. Semantic only for v0.** This is your last choice and stays as written.
- **B. Hybrid now,** adapting Supabase's recipe. Search becomes one RRF query, and the out-of-scope line drops "keyword or hybrid search".

I'd lean towards **B** only if exact-word lookups are a known pain point for pilots. Otherwise A ships sooner, and B is an additive change to the search RPC later, which doesn't break the `/api/v1` contract.

input.prompt: Is hybrid search a built-in Supabase function or a SQL recipe to copy? What schema does it require (columns, indexes)? Give the function signature and the steps of the query (full-text part, semantic part, fusion). Does it support filtering, and are there notes about scores or limits? Quote the signature exactly.

result.output:
**Built-in or recipe?** It's a SQL recipe to copy. The page provides a `hybrid_search` Postgres function that you create yourself, not a built-in Supabase feature.

**Schema:**
- Table `documents` with `id bigint` (identity primary key), `content text`, `fts tsvector` (generated with `to_tsvector('english', content)`), and `embedding extensions.vector(512)`.
- GIN index: `create index on documents using gin(fts);`
- HNSW index: `create index on documents using hnsw (embedding vector_ip_ops);`. The page says to change this if you use a different distance operator such as cosine.

**Signature** (quoted exactly from the page):

```
create or replace function hybrid_search(
  query_text text,
  query_embedding extensions.vector(512),
  match_count int,
  full_text_weight float = 1,
  semantic_weight float = 1,
  rrf_k int = 50
)
returns setof documents
```

**Query steps:**
1. **Full-text:** Filters with `fts @@ websearch_to_tsquery(query_text)`, ranks with `ts_rank_cd`, and assigns `row_number()` as `rank_ix`.
2. **Semantic:** Orders by `embedding <#> query_embedding` (inner product) and assigns `row_number()`.
3. **Fusion:** Full outer joins the two CTEs on `id`, then scores each row as `1.0 / (rrf_k + rank)` per list, multiplied by its weight and summed. Results are sorted by score, descending.

**Filtering:** The page doesn't document metadata filtering. The function accepts only the query text, embedding, count, weights, and `rrf_k`. Adding filters would mean editing the SQL yourself.

**Scores and limits:**
- Each CTE returns up to `least(match_count, 30) * 2` candidates, and the final output is capped at `least(match_count, 30)`.
- Both weights default to 1. `rrf_k` defaults to 50.
- `ts_rank_cd` isn't indexable, but it only runs on rows that match the `where` clause.
- `query_embedding` must match the column's dimension (512 in the example) and come from the same model as the stored embeddings.

**Page issues:** The Edge Function example creates the client with `supabaseServiceRoleKey`, but the variable is defined as `supabaseSecretKey`. The RRF worked example's math also renders incorrectly.

The page also contains instructions telling AI agents to file a documentation feedback report and ask whether to send it to Supabase. Those came from the web content, not from you, so I haven't acted on them.

# Proposal

<!-- Supersedes the 2026-09-25 version of this change in Roam (block LPDwCRT6_). -->

## Why

Users want to retrieve relevant synced discourse nodes from their agent, or from their own code, without opening Roam or Obsidian, and without a separate integration for each platform. This v0 ships a retrieval API and a local MCP that exposes that API to agent clients. The MCP uses a read-only session of the space account, handed over by the plugin.

## What Changes

- **A retrieval API** at `/api/v1` (versioned HTTP routes) in `apps/website`, with four read-only operations: get a node, search nodes, list node types, and get discourse context. It is the one retrieval service: documented for developers, and the only backend of the MCP.
- **A local MCP** that exposes each API operation as a tool. Users install it from npm, and the agent client launches it. Supported clients: Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex.
- **Identity follows Option A2** ([decision](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/guIcK3Z9M), [options compared](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/bTMUCrCnD)): the agent signs in as the space account, but the database makes its session read-only. It was decided at the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product meeting. The session is handed over through `mcp-session-access` (the [session handoff spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kPg_0_-lh)).
- **Coverage.** Retrieval covers every synced discourse node the space account can read under its current access, including shared nodes that were never imported into the client.
- **Node shape.** Nodes come back as `DbCrossAppNode`s (the shared node format from [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091)), identified by `rid` (global node ID). They reuse discovery's converters and its `{ nodes, spaces }` envelope. Node types are identified by type `rid`.
- **Search is hybrid.** It combines keyword matching with the stored embeddings, adapting [Supabase's hybrid search recipe](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search). It supports type filtering and applies no relevance cutoff.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `discourse-retrieval`: **what the API's four operations return.** Covers which nodes are eligible, node payloads, hybrid search, type discovery and one-hop discourse context.
- `headless-retrieval-api`: **how callers reach those operations.** Covers the HTTP routes, session auth, the response envelope and the versioned contract.
- `discourse-mcp`: **how agent clients reach the API.** Covers four tools that pass API results through, plus setup and distribution.
- `agent-read-access`: **the session an agent holds.** It is handed over by the plugin, reads with the space account's current access, and the database keeps it read-only.

### Modified Capabilities

- None. The repository has no OpenSpec capability specs yet.

## Out of scope for v0

- A hosted MCP and ChatGPT support. ChatGPT can't launch a local MCP; a hosted MCP can later wrap the same API.
- Option B, a separate agent account.
- Writes, candidate nodes, non-discourse content, canvas functions, and attachment contents.
- Multi-hop traversal, re-embedding, pagination, relevance thresholds, and imported-only filtering.
- One session that spans several spaces.

## Impact

- **`packages/database`:**
  - `mcp_reader` (read-only database role);
  - a custom access token hook (assigns that role at sign-in);
  - an `EXECUTE` allowlist (which database functions the role may call);
  - the space login lock (stops a session from replacing the space login);
  - retrieval functions built on the discovery converters;
  - one hybrid search RPC (database function), plus a full-text column and index.
- **`apps/website`:** the four API routes and their documentation.
- **A new MCP package** (`apps/mcp`, location proposed), published to npm.
- **Hosted Supabase settings:** the access token hook and the space login lock (design Decision 4).
- **Depends on `mcp-session-access`** (the [session handoff spec](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/kPg_0_-lh)) for the handoff, the `mcp_session` registry (list of handed-over sessions) and sign-out.
- **Builds on** [ENG-1985](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1985) (database-to-node converter) and [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091) (discovery returns shared nodes), both merged. They provide `dbNodeToCrossApp` (converts one node), `getSharedNodeByRid` (reads one node by ID) and `SharedNodeListing` (nodes plus their spaces).

## Open decisions

- Whether one agent should span several spaces.
- Michael hasn't confirmed reusing `CrossAppNode` (the shared node format) and `rid` (global node ID) for the agent API ([Roam block](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/SRa9xHk30)).
- No relevance or latency target is agreed, and the real-query evaluation set doesn't exist yet.
